title: Miscellaneous Resources
description: Additional student resources, including fitness, recreation, and graduate support services.

blocks.body: A comprehensive fitness facility offering a pool, weight room, indoor track, and various drop-in classes, catering to all fitness levels in a supportive environment.

blocks.imageAlt: Goldring Centre for High Performance Sport

blocks.body: State-of-the-art facility featuring a multi-purpose arena, strength and conditioning center, and specialized training spaces for both recreational users and high-performance athletes.
Historic multi-sport facility including gymnasiums, pools, and a strength training area, supporting academic learning, recreational activities, and competitive sports.

cards.title: Centre for Graduate Mentorship and Supervision (CGMS)

blocks.body: The Centre for Graduate Mentorship and Supervision (CGMS) offers support for students who may be experiencing challenges with their supervisors. They provide resources like coaching and workshops focused on improving communication and resolving conflicts, helping you navigate difficult relationships and foster a more productive academic environment. If you're feeling uncertain about your supervisory situation, CGMS can be a valuable ally in finding constructive solutions.

sections.title: Food Support
intro: Free food on and near the St. George campus. Hours change each term, so check each page before you go.

blocks.body: Free groceries for St. George students, Fridays by appointment. Bookings open each Wednesday morning. You need a Daily Bread client ID; bring your TCard and reusable bags.
A free prepared frozen meal every Tuesday at lunchtime, first come, first served. Not running in the summer.
A free weekly meal on St. George campus, started by U of T PhD students and co-funded by the graduate students’ union. Check Instagram for this week’s time and place.
Find a food bank near where you live. This is also where you get the Daily Bread client ID the UTSU Food Bank asks for.
A directory of free and low-cost meals, food banks and food delivery across Toronto.

items.label: Free and low-cost meals near campus →

blocks.body: If an unexpected expense leaves you short of money for food or rent, the School of Graduate Studies offers emergency grants. Talk to your department or SGS financial advising first. Applications aren’t accepted August 1 to October 30.

sections.title: Getting Around
intro: Student transit discounts and other ways to get to campus. Most transit discounts are for full-time students.

blocks.body: Full-time U of T students can buy a discounted TTC monthly pass. First get a TTC Post-Secondary Photo ID card at Bathurst Station or when the TTC visits campus each fall, then have the student fare set on your PRESTO card at Shoppers Drug Mart. Paying per ride costs the regular adult fare.
Full-time students save 40% on GO trains and buses and on the UP Express to Pearson airport. Apply online for a GO Student ID each school year and add it to your PRESTO card.
U of T students get 20% off an annual Bike Share membership, half-price e-bike minutes and no unlock fees.

items.label: U of T Bike Share discount →

blocks.body: Bike racks and lanes, City bike lockers near campus, nearby subway stops and car share, from U of T Transportation Services.
A free escort from Campus Safety to anywhere on campus or a nearby TTC station, 24/7. Request one in the UofT Safety App or by phone.
